title.narrative: Activity under preparation Solid waste management programme for a Circular Economy and Sustainable infrastructure

description.narrative: Despite positive improvements in the regulatory field, solid waste management is an area of growing concern in Peru, especially in large urban areas. Currently, 61% of unrecoverable waste ends up in the country¿s landfills and the total recycling rate is less than 2.5%. Most of the urban solid waste is being dumped in unmanaged dumpsites without adequate treatment, leading to health and environmental long lasting consequences.While the ongoing programme ¿Sustainable Business-A Circular, Inclusive Economy¿ strengthens the enabling environment for Peru¿s transition to a circular economy, this Action aims to focus on one of the most important challenges to circularity: solid waste management. It will support the adaptation of norms in and promote investments in the sector. In Peru, the General Law of Solid Waste[1] introduces the principle of circular economy and diversifies the solid waste management strategies: i) develops cleaner production agreements for solid waste; ii) strengthens the mechanism of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), iii) obliges the implementation of gradual segregation plans, among others[2]. Its implementation is supervised by the Ministry of Environment(MINAM) while Provincial authorities and district municipalities are responsible for ensuring the proper implementation of norms at local levels and the provision of public cleaning services that cover the collection, transport and treat solid waste.' DL ¿ 1278 Integrated Solid Waste Management approved on December 23, 2016 amended in 2020 (DL ¿1501 ), 2022 (DS ¿ 001 -2022-MINAM) and 2023 (Law ¿ 31896).[2] DL ¿. 1501 of May 2020 eliminates the gradual segregation and recycling and makes this activity mandatory.
